person: Walt Brenner is 66 and owns a 24-person field-services firm (surveying and renovation crews in three states). He is the trustee of the company 401(k) and handles HR himself with a part-time bookkeeper, Donna. His new CPA firm sent an email about late 401(k) deposits for the third quarter that he did not finish reading, and he printed the part he understood. He is not a computer person, wants to know what is owed and what it costs, and is wary of anyone selling him something, since a past 'compliance' add-on cost him monthly and missed the one notice that mattered.
stated_up_front: My new CPA's email says some of my 401(k) deposits for the third quarter went in late and I may owe the lost earnings. I'm not a computer person, so tell me which ones are actually late and what it costs me, and don't pay anything until I say.

facts.truth: Brenner Field Services, 24 employees, 401(k) held at Retireline; Walt is trustee.
Paid every other Friday through Paywise Payroll; the Q3 paydays run from 3 July through 25 September, with the next payroll on 2 October not yet deposited.
Two employee deferrals from the 14 August payroll were deposited after the seventh business day; the 14 August deferrals were put in on 28 August.
Three employee loan repayments were deposited late; one shows only on Retireline's separate loan list, not on the deposit log.
Labor Day was Monday, 7 September; the 28 August payroll deposit landed on the seventh business day counting Labor Day as no business day, so it is on time.
The Q3 employer match was deposited in October; Walt thinks it is not a late deferral.
One crew lead, Dale, stopped his deferral in August, so nothing was due for him after that.
A recovery firm in Retireline's offers list wants a quarter of the lost earnings with a minimum fee far above what is owed; Walt wants nothing to do with it.
Walt has the printed payroll stubs and the CPA's email; his EIN is on his payroll stub, and his bank statements come on paper each month.
His rental LLC has its own small plan, which is separate and not part of this check.

unknowns: How many business days after payday a 401(k) deposit has to be made, and why the payroll firm's practice matters.
How the lost earnings are figured, including the rate used.
Which of the five late items is the one only on the loan list, and what an amount is for each.
Whether the match deposited in October counts as late or what its deadline is.
